title: Atrial myxoma: scattered cells in a mucopolysaccharide stroma
vignette: A 22-year-old woman comes to the office due to worsening dyspnea. The patient has also experienced low-grade fevers, a 6.8-kg (15-lb) weight loss, and syncopal episodes over the last 3 months. Her shortness of breath worsens when sitting and improves when lying down. Temperature is 37.4 C (99.3 F), blood pressure is 115/72 mm Hg, pulse is 75/min and regular, and respirations are 12/min. The lungs are clear. Cardiac auscultation reveals a low-pitched, mid-diastolic rumble at the cardiac apex. The remainder of the physical examination is normal. ECG reveals left atrial enlargement, and echocardiography shows a large, pedunculated mass in the left atrium. Histologic analysis of this mass will most likely reveal which of the following?

clues.note: Constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss) can accompany atrial myxoma, which may secrete cytokines such as interleukin-6.

clues.text: worsens when sitting and improves when lying down
clues.note: POSITION-dependent symptoms are characteristic of a mobile, pedunculated atrial mass that intermittently obstructs the mitral valve (a 'ball-valve' effect).

clues.text: low-pitched, mid-diastolic rumble at the cardiac apex
clues.note: A mid-diastolic rumble at the apex reflects obstruction of left-atrial outflow across the mitral valve - mimicking mitral stenosis.

clues.text: large, pedunculated mass in the left atrium
clues.note: A pedunculated LEFT ATRIAL mass is the classic location/appearance of a cardiac myxoma, the most common primary cardiac tumor.

whatMatters: A pedunculated LEFT ATRIAL mass causing position-dependent mitral obstruction (mid-diastolic rumble) with constitutional symptoms = cardiac MYXOMA, the most common primary cardiac tumor. Histology shows SCATTERED (myxoma) CELLS within a gelatinous MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDE (myxoid) STROMA. Answer D.
strategy: Identify atrial myxoma from location (left atrium), pedunculated mobility (position-dependent obstruction/'tumor plop'), and constitutional/embolic features, then recall its histology: sparse stellate/myxoma cells in an abundant mucopolysaccharide stroma. Reject infective endocarditis histologies (fungal hyphae, gram-positive cocci - unlikely without valve disease/IV drug use), AML (malignant myeloid cells), and nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (platelet-fibrin vegetations).

options.text: Scattered cells within a mucopolysaccharide stroma
Solid mass of platelets and fibrin

eliminations.label: Branching septate hyphae - fungal endocarditis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: septate branching hyphae (e.g., Aspergillus) = fungal endocarditis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this young woman has a pedunculated atrial MASS (myxoma), not valvular vegetations from fungal infection. ✅ Correct if: fungal endocarditis (immunocompromised/prosthetic valve).

eliminations.label: Gram-positive cocci in clusters - bacterial endocarditis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: staphylococcal (gram-positive cocci in clusters) endocarditis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: endocarditis produces valvular vegetations with a regurgitant murmur, not a pedunculated atrial mass with a diastolic rumble; no risk factors here. ✅ Correct if: infective endocarditis with vegetations.

eliminations.label: Malignant myeloid cells - acute myeloid leukemia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sheets of malignant myeloid blasts (AML), which rarely infiltrate the heart. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: AML presents with cytopenias/marrow failure, not a solitary pedunculated atrial mass. ✅ Correct if: leukemic cardiac infiltration with systemic AML.

eliminations.label: Platelet-fibrin mass - nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sterile platelet-fibrin vegetations (marantic endocarditis), seen in advanced malignancy/lupus. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: those are small valvular vegetations that embolize, not a large pedunculated atrial tumor. ✅ Correct if: nonbacterial thrombotic (marantic) endocarditis.

reasoning: Pedunculated LEFT ATRIAL mass with position-dependent mitral obstruction + constitutional symptoms = cardiac myxoma
Myxomas are the most common primary cardiac tumor (usually left atrium)
Histology: scattered stellate 'myxoma' cells within an abundant gelatinous mucopolysaccharide stroma
-> scattered cells within a mucopolysaccharide stroma; answer D
mechanism: Cardiac MYXOMA is the most common PRIMARY cardiac tumor, and about 80% arise in the LEFT ATRIUM (typically pedunculated, attached near the fossa ovalis). A mobile, pedunculated left atrial myxoma can intermittently prolapse into and obstruct the mitral valve ('ball-valve' effect), producing a low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble that mimics mitral stenosis and causes POSITION-dependent dyspnea/syncope and an early diastolic 'tumor plop.' Fragments may embolize (stroke, limb ischemia), and cytokine secretion (e.g., interleukin-6) can cause constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss). HISTOLOGICALLY, myxomas show SCATTERED (sparse) stellate or globular 'myxoma cells' embedded in an abundant, gelatinous MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDE (myxoid) STROMA with blood vessels and areas of hemorrhage (hemosiderin). This benign appearance distinguishes it from the distractors: infective endocarditis (fungal hyphae or gram-positive cocci on valves), acute myeloid leukemia (malignant myeloid cells), and nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (platelet-fibrin vegetations).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid CV > cardiac myxoma: most common primary cardiac tumor, ~80% left atrium, pedunculated; mid-diastolic rumble/'tumor plop', position-dependent obstruction, embolization, IL-6 constitutional symptoms; histology = scattered cells in myxoid (mucopolysaccharide) stroma.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Pedunculated left atrial mass with positional mitral obstruction = myxoma -> myxoid stroma histology.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on myxoma, pedunculated, mid-diastolic rumble/tumor plop, mucopolysaccharide/myxoid stroma, or ball-valve effect? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Fungal hyphae/gram-positive cocci = endocarditis; malignant myeloid cells = AML; platelet-fibrin = marantic endocarditis - not a myxoma.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: atrial myxoma = most common primary cardiac tumor; left atrium; scattered cells in myxoid stroma; positional obstruction + IL-6 symptoms.

keywords.front: Pedunculated left atrial mass + positional mitral obstruction
keywords.back: Cardiac myxoma (most common primary cardiac tumor)
Scattered (stellate) cells in a mucopolysaccharide (myxoid) stroma

CV > tumor plop, embolization, IL-6 constitutional symptoms.

memoryHook: A myxoma is a jelly-on-a-stalk in the left atrium: it swings into the mitral valve (rumble that changes with position) and, under the microscope, is a few lonely cells adrift in gooey mucopolysaccharide.
